Immune Dysregulation Subgroup Proportions in Critically Ill Patients
=====================================================================

Dataset: subspace_score_table.csv (3,948 samples, 6 cohorts)
Definition of critically ill: severity == "severe" (includes Severe and Fatal grades)
Subgroup classification: 2x2 grid of myeloid_z_score and lymphoid_z_score, threshold z ≈ 1.65

Primary Result (n = 1,798 critically ill patients):
-----------------------------------------------------
  system-wide dysregulation:      1,161 / 1,798 = 64.6%  (95% CI: 62.3%–66.7%)
  lymphoid dysregulation:           348 / 1,798 = 19.4%  (95% CI: 17.6%–21.2%)
  balanced:                         150 / 1,798 =  8.3%  (95% CI: 7.2%–9.7%)
  myeloid dysregulation:            139 / 1,798 =  7.7%  (95% CI: 6.6%–9.1%)

Interpretation:
Nearly two-thirds (64.6%) of critically ill patients exhibit system-wide immune
dysregulation — elevated activity in both myeloid and lymphoid programs. An
additional 19.4% show isolated lymphoid dysregulation. Only 8.3% of critically
ill patients retain a balanced immune profile, compared to 46.9% of non-severe
patients and 92.2% of healthy controls.

By severity grade within critically ill:
  Severe (n=1,203):  system-wide 61.3%, lymphoid 20.5%, balanced 8.7%, myeloid 9.4%
  Fatal   (n=387):   system-wide 69.5%, lymphoid 17.6%, balanced 9.6%, myeloid 3.4%

Fatal cases have a higher rate of system-wide dysregulation (69.5% vs 61.3%)
and a lower rate of isolated myeloid dysregulation (3.4% vs 9.4%) compared
to non-fatal severe cases (chi-squared = 18.06, p = 4.3 × 10⁻⁴).

The specialist agent (`tabular_genomics_analyst`) has completed the analysis. Here is the summary:

**Immune Dysregulation Subgroup Proportions Among Critically Ill Patients (n = 1,798)**

| Subgroup | n | Proportion | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| system-wide dysregulation | 1,161 | 64.6% | [62.3%, 66.7%] |
| lymphoid dysregulation | 348 | 19.4% | [17.6%, 21.2%] |
| balanced | 150 | 8.3% | [7.2%, 9.7%] |
| myeloid dysregulation | 139 | 7.7% | [6.6%, 9.1%] |

The subgroups were classified using a 2x2 grid of myeloid and lymphoid z-scores with a threshold of z > ~1.65 (approximately the 95th percentile of a standard normal), separating high from low activity in each compartment. Within critically ill patients, fatal cases showed higher system-wide dysregulation (69.5% vs 61.3%, chi-squared p = 4.3 x 10^-4).

Both required output files (`trace.md` and `answer.txt`) have been written to the workspace directory.
